title: Right Heart Injury Monitoring on ECMO
official: Feasibility Study for Monitoring Right Ventricular Injury in Patients With Severe Acute Respiratory Failure Supported With Veno-venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
summary:
This study aims to find out whether it is practical to introduce a consistent monitoring approach to the right side of the heart in patients supported with VV-ECMO.

VV-ECMO is a life support machine that takes over the work of the lungs to give them time to recover. It is used when lung injury is life-threatening.

Whilst receiving VV-ECMO support, in addition to the current standard of care, the following will be performed twice weekly:

* Heart scan (echocardiogram)
* Blood tests (hs-troponin and NT-proBNP)

The patient's involvement in the study lasts for as long as they are on the life support machine, plus one final heart scan 48 hours after it is removed.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults (≥18 years old)
* Less than 72 hours after being established on VV-ECMO due to SARF (either retrieved to RPH from another hospital or already an inpatient at RPH)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients \<18 years old
* Patients that had been previously included in this study
* Patients requiring VV-ECMO support post pulmonary thrombo-endarterectomy, as a bridge to lung transplantation or post lung-transplantation
* Any other reason for VV-ECMO support that is not SARF
* Patients and/or Personal Consultee not fluent in English
